description:
## Why this issue exists

Stoa makes outbound TLS connections for: SMTP relay, IPFS/Kubo API, OIDC discovery, and any external webhook or ActivityPub delivery. It is not verified that all outbound clients use a verified certificate chain (no `danger_accept_invalid_certs`, no custom trust store that bypasses CA validation).

An auditor will ask for evidence that all outbound connections validate server certificates. A misconfigured outbound client enables MITM attacks.

## What needs to be done

- Audit every `reqwest::Client` construction site and every direct `tokio-rustls` client setup.
- Confirm no code path uses `.danger_accept_invalid_certs(true)` in non-test code.
- Confirm no code path uses a trust store that does not include the system root CAs or a pinned well-known CA.
- If any dev-mode flag bypasses cert validation, gate it behind the env classification from the dev mode guard epic.
- Add a CI test that spins up a server with a self-signed cert and verifies outbound connection is rejected in production mode.

## Acceptance criteria

- No `danger_accept_invalid_certs` in non-test code
- All `reqwest::Client` and rustls `ClientConfig` constructions audited and documented
- Self-signed server rejected in production mode
- Any dev-mode bypass is guarded and logs a warning

## Design notes

Regulatory refs: All frameworks — outbound cert validation is universally required. SOC2 CC6.7, PCI-DSS 4.2.1.
title: Outbound TLS certificate validation audit
